body:
## Goal

Maintainer-authorized, narrowly scoped proof: can ty statically reject unsupported ordering/range operations (starting with ZonedDatetime) without unacceptable declaration or typing drawbacks?

Use subagents for isolated positive/negative consumer probes. Investigate ty intersections/narrowing and conventional descriptor/capability/self typing. Preserve equality/membership, supported-column ordering, field value/result types, and ordinary declaration ergonomics. Check exact diagnostics; no Any-based evasion, blanket optionality, or runtime-only guard presented as static success.

Research only, no production API changes, backend execution, or broad capability redesign. Start from current origin/main. Deliver evidence, limitations and a promising minimal direction, not a full implementation.

The maintainer explicitly requested subagent-led feasibility research. Public seams are ty-checked positive/negative consumer examples for column declarations, field/result typing, equality/membership and ordering/range/aggregate calls. No production changes or backend tests. Two independent angles: ty intersections/narrowing and conventional restricted-self/capability/descriptor typing. Child work is isolated to temporary probe directories; durable findings will be recorded on this branch.

title: Prove static rejection of unsupported column ordering with ty
